title: [CQ-R13h] Certify cancellation and recovery probes
description:
Objective: add certify checks showing, on real hardware, that a cancelled run tears down cleanly and that a crashed controller's VM is recovered. Both are in CQ-R13's objective: cancellation and recovery.

Split out of CQ-R13 (task-f4811a72) by architect-e4b7eee0 on 2026-10-30. It depends on CQ-R13f, for the edit order on certify.mjs.

Deliverable: two checks appended to CERTIFY_CHECKS, each in its own VM.
- 'cancellation': runCheckJob with an approved command that blocks, and an AbortSignal that fires once the session has started. The run must resolve with VM 'deleted', an outcome other than 'passed', and no live ledger record of its attempt.
- 'recovery':
  - A child node process runs a provisioning, and this check SIGKILLs it once the VM is launched. The child is spawned with process.execPath and a fixed module argument, never a shell.
  - Then, in the parent, lifecycle reconcile and cleanupOwned, with the child's attempt closed, must delete exactly that VM.
  - A foreign VM record present in the same ledger must survive.

Every timing bound is a fixed constant, and every outcome maps to a fixed code.

Tests in scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs use fake providers and fake child processes. The native behavior is certified only by the operator run.

Out of scope:
- the canary toolchain check (CQ-R13g);
- enabling verified-local;
- .moe edits.

Verification command (fresh, exit 0 required): node --test scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs (on WSL: env -i with the nvm Node 24 PATH)
definitionOfDone: 'cancellation' passes only when an aborted check run resolves without 'passed', with its VM deleted and no live ledger record of its attempt. Shown by tests.
'recovery' passes only when, after its controller child is SIGKILLed mid-provision, reconcile and cleanup delete exactly that orphaned VM and leave a foreign record intact. Shown by tests.
The child process is spawned without a shell, with a fixed argv, and is always reaped. Shown by tests.
The verification command exits 0 with its output supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

implementationPlan.description:
TESTS FIRST (red). Load test-driven-development.

Edit the LANDED bytes. These land first, in order:
- CQ-R13d: certify.mjs, with run(context) checks and the CF rows;
- CQ-R13e1/CQ-R13e: certify-bridge.mjs, BRIDGE_CHECKS, certifySnapshot(), the context.bounds and deps.bounds mechanism, and the harness's materialize and check-session spawn fakes;
- CQ-R13f: its own checks;
- CQ-R11e: runCheckJob with a required `dependencies` and injectable toolchain/installToolchain steps.
Re-read certify.mjs, certify-bridge.mjs, check-lifecycle.mjs and the certify rows of scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs first.

THE HARNESS. In scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs, extend the certify harness with:
- deps.checkSteps: { toolchain: <resolves a frozen {file, sha256: 64 hex, size, version}>, installToolchain: <resolves> }, so no test downloads Node.
- deps.spawn: a fake child factory. Each fake child is an EventEmitter with a Writable stdin that records its bytes. kill(signal) records the signal and emits 'close' (null, signal) on setImmediate, unless the row says it hangs.
- A per-row onInput hook that sees the child's parsed stdin JSON. The default simulates the child's provisioning: ledger.reserve(owner), then update to 'launching' and then 'owned', and fake.present.set(instance, 'Running').
- deps.bounds with small cancelBudgetMs, launchMs, pollMs and reapMs, and deps.sleep resolving at once.

ROWS (each failure row asserts the fixed code via the report's checks entry, and asserts that teardown still passed):
- LC1, cancellation passes.
  - Exactly one check session runs, with frame {id:'certify-cancel', command:'echo ready; exec sleep 600', protected:[]}.
  - Its stdin was destroyed right after its first stdout bytes: the abort.
  - runCheckJob resolved outcome 'infra-failure' and vm 'deleted'.
  - ledger.read(<its instance>).phase is 'deleted'.
  - The instance differs from certify's main VM, which is still 'owned'.
- LC2, cancellation fail mapping. Each row uses injected deps.checkSteps:
  - The session step resolves without ever calling its provider.spawn: CERTIFY_CANCEL_NOT_STARTED.
  - The session step calls input.provider.spawn and pushes stdout bytes, then resolves {outcome:'passed', exitCode:0, signal:null, outputTail:''}: CERTIFY_CANCEL_PASSED.
  - The fake delete fails, so vm is 'delete-failed': CERTIFY_CANCEL_VM_NOT_DELETED.
  - A remove step resolves 'deleted' without touching the ledger: CERTIFY_CANCEL_RECORD_LIVE.
  - An onReady-style runCheckJob rejection keeps its own stable code.
- LC3, recovery passes.
  - kill('SIGKILL') was called exactly once, after the child's record reached 'owned', and 'close' was awaited.
  - The delete recorder shows exactly the child's instance deleted, and its record is 'deleted'.
  - The foreign record the check seeded is not 'deleted', and no delete targeted it.
  - certify's main VM is still 'owned'.
- LC4, spawn contract.
  - spawn was called exactly once, as (process.execPath, [RECOVERY_CHILD], { shell: false, windowsHide: true, stdio: ['pipe', 'ignore', 'ignore'] }). RECOVERY_CHILD equals path.join(<scripts/local-runner>, 'certify-recovery-child.mjs').
  - stdin received exactly one JSON line, {ledgerDir, cacheDir, owner}, and was ended.
- LC5, recovery fail mapping. Every row awaits the child's 'close' and ends with no live child VM, because the check's finally deleteOwned removed it:
  - the child closes before 'owned': CERTIFY_RECOVERY_CHILD_EXITED;
  - no 'owned' record within the launchMs/pollMs poll budget: a kill, then CERTIFY_RECOVERY_NOT_LAUNCHED;
  - a child that never closes after the kill: CERTIFY_RECOVERY_NOT_REAPED after reapMs;
  - spawn throws, or the child emits 'error': CERTIFY_RECOVERY_SPAWN_FAILED;
  - the fake delete fails for the child's VM: CERTIFY_RECOVERY_CLEANUP_FAILED.
- LC6, the REAL child module. Spawned as process.execPath certify-recovery-child.mjs, without a shell, it exits 64 within 10 s, with empty stdout and stderr, for each of these on stdin:
  - '';
  - 'x';
  - '{}';
  - an extra key;
  - a relative ledgerDir;
  - a control character in cacheDir;
  - an owner that fails validOwner;
  - more than 4096 bytes.
- LC7, composition.
  - The ids of CERTIFY_CHECKS end [..., 'cancellation', 'recovery', 'teardown'].
  - The all-pass CF1 row passes.
  - Each new deps.bounds key outside 1..its constant is CERTIFY_INPUT_INVALID before any provider call.

scripts/tests/local-runner-bundle.test.mjs: `shipped` (NOT `required`, which the onboarding refusal row walks) gains 'certify-lifecycle.mjs' and 'certify-recovery-child.mjs'.

Run `node --test scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs scripts/tests/local-runner-bundle.test.mjs`. The new rows fail and every other row passes.

ERROR HANDLING in the tests: assert fixed codes, never messages. Remove every scratch directory in t.after, and close every fake child.

implementationPlan.description:
Create scripts/local-runner/certify-recovery-child.mjs: the recovery check's controller child.

HEADER COMMENT
- It runs one real provisioning, which the certify parent SIGKILLs once the VM is launched, so that reconcile and cleanup are certified on a real orphan.
- Its argv is fixed: [process.execPath, this file].
- Its only input is one JSON line on stdin, {ledgerDir, cacheDir, owner}.
- It prints nothing.
- Exit codes: 0 provisioned (the parent normally kills it first), 64 bad input, 70 any provisioning failure.

BEHAVIOR
1. Read stdin up to 4097 bytes. More than 4096 bytes exits 64.
2. JSON.parse it. The result must be a record with exactly the keys ledgerDir, cacheDir and owner.
   - Both dirs are absolute strings with no control character (/[\x00-\x1f\x7f]/).
   - owner passes lifecycle.mjs validOwner.
   - Anything else exits 64 BEFORE any import of a platform module or any provider call.
3. Then it calls provisionGuest({ platform: platformFor(process.platform), ledger: createLedger(ledgerDir), owner, cacheDir, supervisor: <the REAL bytes of ./guest-supervisor.py via readFile(new URL(..., import.meta.url))>, credential: randomBytes(32) }).
   - A null platformFor, a throw, or provisioned !== true exits 70.
   - provisioned === true exits 0.

ERROR HANDLING
- Every path ends in process.exitCode plus a natural exit, or an explicit exit with a fixed code.
- No stack, path or credential byte is ever printed.
- The credential never leaves this process.
implementationPlan.note: Created certify-recovery-child.mjs. It reads at most 4096 bytes of stdin; over that is 64. It takes exactly the {cacheDir, ledgerDir, owner} keys, with absolute control-free dirs and validOwner, and copies the owner; anything else is 64. cli.mjs and provision.mjs are imported dynamically only after validation. It provisions with platformFor(process.platform), the real supervisor bytes and its own randomBytes(32) credential: provisioned is 0, a null platform, a throw or not provisioned is 70. Every path ends in an explicit process.exit with a fixed code, and nothing is printed. LC6 green: all 8 bad inputs exit 64 with empty stdout and stderr, and the scratch dir stays empty.

implementationPlan.description:
Create scripts/local-runner/certify-lifecycle.mjs with the 'cancellation' check. The 'recovery' check follows in the next step.

EXPORTS
- LIFECYCLE_BOUNDS = Object.freeze({ cancelBudgetMs: 300_000, launchMs: 900_000, pollMs: 1_000, reapMs: 30_000 }).
- LIFECYCLE_CHECKS: frozen [cancellation, recovery] entries in R13d's frozen {id, run(context)} shape.
- RECOVERY_CHILD = fileURLToPath(new URL('./certify-recovery-child.mjs', import.meta.url)).

CONTEXT
The check reads these from context: name (certify's main VM, never touched here), platform (the observed platform), ledger (the base ledger, not the capturing wrapper), cacheDir, supervisor (the real bytes), provider, bounds, and deps.checkSteps (test-only; undefined natively).

'cancellation', in its own VM:
- cancelOwner = { taskId: 'task-certify', attemptId: `attempt-${randomBytes(16).toString('hex')}`, generation: 1 }.
- A controller = new AbortController() and started = false.
- session = input => (steps.session ?? runCheckSession)({ ...input, provider: { ...input.provider, spawn: (...args) => { const child = (input.provider.spawn ?? spawnProcess)(...args); child?.stdout?.once?.('data', () => { started = true; controller.abort(); }); return child; } } }).
  - The trigger wraps only the check session's spawn, never materialize's or verify's. The supervisor writes hello first, so the first stdout bytes mean the session started.
- result = await runCheckJob({ platform, ledger, owner: cancelOwner, cacheDir, supervisor, credential: randomBytes(32), snapshot: certifySnapshot(), check: { id: 'certify-cancel', command: 'echo ready; exec sleep 600', protected: [] }, budgetMs: bounds.cancelBudgetMs, onReady: async () => {}, dependencies: [], provider, signal: controller.signal }, { ...steps, session }).
- Map the result in this order:
  1. !started is CERTIFY_CANCEL_NOT_STARTED. A run that failed for any other reason must never pass vacuously.
  2. result.outcome === 'passed' is CERTIFY_CANCEL_PASSED.
  3. result.vm !== 'deleted' is CERTIFY_CANCEL_VM_NOT_DELETED.
  4. (await ledger.read(result.instance)).phase !== 'deleted' is CERTIFY_CANCEL_RECORD_LIVE. A read failure maps to this code too.
  5. Otherwise the check passes.
- A runCheckJob rejection propagates its own stable code through R13d's wrapper. runCheckJob deletes its VM before it settles, on every path.

ERROR HANDLING
- Fixed codes only.
- The trigger never throws: optional chaining on the child.
- No guest byte reaches the report.
implementationPlan.note: Created certify-lifecycle.mjs with LIFECYCLE_BOUNDS, RECOVERY_CHILD and the 'cancellation' check. Real runCheckJob runs in its own VM: a fresh synthetic owner, certifySnapshot(), the frozen CANCEL_CHECK, budget = bounds.cancelBudgetMs, dependencies [], and an AbortController signal. The abort trigger wraps only the session step's provider.spawn and fires on its first stdout bytes, which also sets started. Mapping order: NOT_STARTED, then PASSED, then VM_NOT_DELETED, then RECORD_LIVE (a ledger read failure maps to RECORD_LIVE). deps.checkSteps is test-only: runCheckJob steps plus `job` (the seam noted in step 1). Exercised once step 5 wires LIFECYCLE_CHECKS into certify.mjs.

implementationPlan.description:
scripts/local-runner/certify-lifecycle.mjs: the 'recovery' check, after 'cancellation'.

SETUP
1. The foreign record. foreignOwner is a fresh synthetic owner. Run foreign = await ledger.reserve(foreignOwner), then update it to { phase: 'launching', launchTries: 1 }, then to { phase: 'owned' }. That is the test helper seed()'s sequence. No VM exists for it, and cleanup must preserve it.
2. childOwner is a fresh synthetic owner.
3. Spawn the child: child = (deps.spawn ?? spawn)(process.execPath, [RECOVERY_CHILD], { shell: false, windowsHide: true, stdio: ['pipe', 'ignore', 'ignore'] }).
   - A throw, or an 'error' event, is CERTIFY_RECOVERY_SPAWN_FAILED.
   - Track closed = once('close').
4. Write JSON.stringify({ ledgerDir, cacheDir, owner: childOwner }) + '\n' to stdin, then end it. ledgerDir is the certify ledger's directory (path.join(workDir, 'ledger')) and cacheDir is certify's cacheDir.

THE WATCH
Poll at most ceil(launchMs / pollMs) times, sleeping with deps.sleep ?? timers/promises setTimeout(pollMs):
- If the child closed, it is CERTIFY_RECOVERY_CHILD_EXITED.
- record = (await ledger.list()).records.find(r => r.attemptId === childOwner.attemptId). If its phase is 'owned', stop polling.
- When the polls are exhausted, kill and fail with CERTIFY_RECOVERY_NOT_LAUNCHED.

THE KILL
child.kill('SIGKILL'). Then await closed, bounded by reapMs. No close within that bound is CERTIFY_RECOVERY_NOT_REAPED.

THE RECOVERY
1. await reconcileOwned({ ledger, provider }).
2. report = await cleanupOwned({ ledger, provider, attemptPhase: id => (id === childOwner.attemptId ? 'closed' : null), leaseHeld: () => false }).
3. It passes only when ALL of these hold:
   - report.deleted deep-equals [record.instance];
   - report.errors is empty;
   - the child record now reads phase 'deleted';
   - the foreign record's phase is not 'deleted'.
   Otherwise it is CERTIFY_RECOVERY_CLEANUP_FAILED.
   certify's main VM and the cancellation record are never deleted here: the main VM's attempt reads null, and 'deleted' is not a launched phase.

FINALLY, ON EVERY PATH
- If the child has not closed, kill it and await the bounded close.
- If the child's record exists and is not 'deleted', call deleteOwned({ ledger, name: record.instance, owner: childOwner, provider }) and swallow its result. No real VM may leak, but this cleanup never turns a failure into a pass.

The parent kills the child alone (TerminateProcess on Windows), as a crashed controller would leave it. Grandchild multipass probes end on their own bounded timeouts.

ERROR HANDLING
- Fixed codes only. Every await is bounded.
- The child is always reaped.
- No guest byte, path or credential reaches the report.
implementationPlan.note:
Added the 'recovery' check, so LIFECYCLE_CHECKS is now [cancellation, recovery].
- Setup: it seeds a foreign record through the ledger API (reserve, launching, owned) and spawns the child as (process.execPath, [RECOVERY_CHILD], {shell:false, windowsHide:true, stdio:['pipe','ignore','ignore']}). A spawn throw is SPAWN_FAILED. stdin gets an 'error' handler, then one JSON line, then end.
- Poll: at most ceil(launchMs/pollMs) times. Order: errored → SPAWN_FAILED, closed → CHILD_EXITED, the record 'owned' → stop. When the polls run out, it fails NOT_LAUNCHED.
- Reap: SIGKILL plus a close wait raced against a timers/promises delay(reapMs), whose timer is aborted afterwards; a miss is NOT_REAPED.
- Recovery: reconcileOwned, then cleanupOwned with attemptPhase 'closed' only for the child's attempt. It passes only when deleted == [child], there are no errors, the child record is 'deleted' and the foreign record is not; any throw is CLEANUP_FAILED.
- finally: reap, then deleteOwned on the child's still-live record, with its result swallowed.
The check reads c.ledgerDir, which step 5 adds to certify's context so the ledger path has a single source.

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW, once, as the final step. Load adversarial-self-review. Read the five-file diff as an attacker.

Cancellation:
- Can it pass when the session never started? `started` must gate it.
- Can the abort trigger fire on materialize's or verify's spawn?

Recovery:

The child:

implementationPlan.note:
I reviewed the five-file diff adversarially.

FIXED: cancellation could pass when the abort was ignored. The 300s budget would turn the run into 'timeout', which is not 'passed', and the VM gets deleted anyway. A 'timeout' outcome now fails as CERTIFY_CANCEL_TIMED_OUT, since runCheckSession maps an abort to infra-failure and only a budget expiry to timeout. LC2 gains that row.

Verified to hold:
- `started` gates the pass.
- Only the session step's spawn is wrapped; materialize and verify get the raw c.provider.
- A run can't pass with its VM or record live (vm==='deleted' plus a ledger read for 'deleted').
- Cleanup deletes only records with the child's attempt closed. Every other attempt reads null, so it is attempt-unknown and preserved. holdReason maps a throwing lookup to unknown, so the main VM, the cancellation record and the foreign record survive. The foreign record is reconciled to 'absent', which is lifecycle's normal behaviour, and is never deleted.
- finally reaps and runs deleteOwned on any non-deleted child record; LAUNCHED includes launching.
- Every wait is bounded: ceil(launchMs/pollMs) polls, reapMs (twice at most), the stdin 'error' handler, and the spawn 'error' handler.
- The child's argv is fixed and its stdin carries only certify's workDir paths and a random owner. It validates (exact keys, absolute control-free dirs, validOwner, 4 KiB cap) before importing cli/provision. Its credential is generated in-process, and its stdout and stderr are ignored.
- Two runs sharing a workDir use random owners and names.

Theoretical, not fixed:
(a) On the NOT_LAUNCHED path, the child is killed mid `multipass launch`. If multipassd completes that launch after finally's deleteOwned found the VM absent, the VM could outlive the check. This is the same window as lifecycle's restart recovery, and launchMs is 15 minutes.
(b) A child that survives SIGKILL past 2×reapMs is left behind. A real process can't do that outside D-state.

Fresh run: exit 0, 346 tests, 345 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped (the opt-in macOS native smoke).

Governor, 20:35Z: LANE SWAP, so idle coders can start (human: "release the dependencies first"). R13h now goes BEFORE R13f. The R13f edge was only "for the edit order on certify.mjs", and R13f (d45d52c0) is still unplanned. It now depends on this row.

Where the plan says "<CQ-R13f's checks>" or "<R13f's bounds, if any>", there are none: BODY = [...R13d's core, ...BRIDGE_CHECKS, ...LIFECYCLE_CHECKS], with 'teardown' kept last. planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- Cancellation abort trigger. Rejected: aborting in onReady, because the session would never start, so that tests pre-session cancellation, not in-session. Also rejected: a timer, which is imprecise. Chosen: wrap ONLY the check session's provider.spawn and fire on its first stdout bytes (hello). A `started` gate keeps a run that failed for another reason from passing vacuously.
- Recovery input channel. Rejected: argv JSON, because the argv must stay fixed. Rejected: env. Chosen: one stdin JSON line. The child generates its own credential, so nothing secret crosses.
- Kill scope. The child is killed alone, not its process group: a SIGKILLed controller leaves exactly that. Grandchild probes are bounded by their own timeouts.
- Foreign record. A launched-phase record ('owned', with no VM) is seeded through the ledger API, as seed() does, so cleanupOwned really evaluates it. A 'reserved' record would be skipped trivially, which would make the test vacuous.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- runCheckJob(input, steps), after CQ-R11e: dependencies is required ([] = no phase). steps include toolchain/installToolchain/session/remove. It deletes its VM before settling on every path, and resolves {outcome, vm, instance, ...}.
- lifecycle.mjs exports createLedger (with list/read/reserve/update), deleteOwned, cleanupOwned({ledger, provider, attemptPhase, leaseHeld}), which deletes only launched records whose attempt is 'closed' and preserves anything unknown, reconcileOwned and validOwner. updateRecord accepts only phase/launchTries changes.
- platformFor (cli.mjs) imports without side effects; native-smoke.mjs imports it the same way.
- The harness pieces come from earlier tasks: fakeVm present-map, a delete recorder, R13e1's materialize and check-session spawn fakes, and R11e's checkHarness step fakes pattern (CJ rows).
planningNotes.risks:
- Edit order: R13f lands its checks in certify.mjs first. Keep BODY's order, and make the bounds keys unique.
- Natively, two VMs run at once: certify's main VM plus the cancellation VM, or plus the recovery VM. The operator host needs room for 2x GUEST_RESOURCES.
- If the cancellation run's toolchain step downloads the pinned Node toolchain into certify's cacheDir on first use, that is expected.
- On Windows, kill('SIGKILL') is TerminateProcess. 'close' still follows, because the child's stdout and stderr are 'ignore'.
- The poll budget is a count (deterministic with an injected sleep), not wall-clock time.

CQ-R13h adds two certify checks, 'cancellation' and 'recovery'. Each runs in its own owned VM, before 'teardown'.

Files:
- certify-lifecycle.mjs (new): LIFECYCLE_BOUNDS {cancelBudgetMs 300000, launchMs 900000, pollMs 1000, reapMs 30000}, RECOVERY_CHILD and LIFECYCLE_CHECKS.
- certify-recovery-child.mjs (new). Its argv is fixed, and its stdin is one JSON line {ledgerDir, cacheDir, owner}. It validates that line before importing cli/provision, so before any provider call, prints nothing, and exits 0, 64 or 70.
- certify.mjs:
  - BOUNDS = {...BRIDGE_BOUNDS, ...LIFECYCLE_BOUNDS} for deps.bounds validation and the native entry;
  - BODY = [core, BRIDGE, CONTAINMENT, LIFECYCLE], then teardown. There are no R13f checks, per the governor's 20:31Z lane-swap comment;
  - the context gains ledgerDir.
- Tests: LC1–LC7 in local-runner.test.mjs, plus the two new modules in the bundle test's `shipped` list.

Cancellation:
- It aborts the run at the session spawn's first stdout bytes.
- It passes only when the session started, the outcome is neither 'passed' nor 'timeout', the VM was deleted and the record reads 'deleted'.

Recovery:
- It seeds a foreign record and spawns the real child (shell:false, [execPath, RECOVERY_CHILD]).
- Once the child's record reads 'owned', it SIGKILLs the child and awaits close, with every wait bounded.
- It then reconciles and runs cleanup with only the child's attempt closed. It passes only when exactly that VM is deleted and the foreign record is not deleted.
- finally always reaps the child and runs deleteOwned on its live record.

- The adversarial review added CERTIFY_CANCEL_TIMED_OUT, so an ignored abort cannot pass on the budget's timeout.
- The test harness clones the fake guest for multi-VM runs.
